problem:
Which of the matrices below are singular?

$$
N=[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}],\,V=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -2 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,Z=[\begin{aligned}0 & 8 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$
worked_solution:
- For the matrix $N$, we have

$$
det(N)=3\cdot 0-0\cdot 1=0.
$$

Because $det(N)=0,$ we conclude that $N$ is not invertible. Since $N$ is a square matrix that is not invertible, we also say that $N$ is singular.

- The matrix $V$ is a $5\times 1$ matrix. So, it is not invertible. Since the matrix is not square, we can't say that it's singular.

- For the matrix $Z$, we have

$$
det(Z)=0\cdot 0-2\cdot 8=-16.
$$

Because $det(Z)\ne 0,$ we conclude that $Z$ is invertible.

Therefore, only $N$ is singular.
